report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/kairos/drafts.py chunk 1/1. All claims in docstrings and comments checked against the code. 11 claims found: 10 kept, 1 uncheckable.
risks: _safe_path | medium | The regex _ID_RE allows '.' which could be a dotfile; but since the path is resolved and checked relative to DRAFT_DIR, traversal is still blocked. Could settle by testing with a dotfile name.
_safe_path | low | The regex allows '-' but a trailing dash after strip might be included; since _safe_path only uses the id as stem, it's safe. Could settle by testing.

set_status | low | The docstring says 'Idempotent' but the code does not check if status is already the same; it still writes the file. Could settle by checking if the status is unchanged and skipping write.

handoff.purpose: Persist advisory drafts as JSON files, with safe path resolution, lifecycle management (save, list, get, delete, set_status, apply_payload).

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Repository root path, computed as parent of current file's grandparent.

symbols.name: DRAFT_DIR
symbols.note: Directory for draft files under runs/drafts.

symbols.name: _SLUG_RE
symbols.note: Regex to replace non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens.

symbols.name: _ID_RE
symbols.note: Regex to validate draft IDs: alphanumeric, dots, underscores, hyphens, max 120 chars.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Converts a string to a slug for use in filenames.

symbols.name: _safe_path
symbols.note: Resolves a draft ID to a safe path inside DRAFT_DIR, or None if unsafe.

symbols.name: save_draft
symbols.note: Writes a draft JSON file to DRAFT_DIR.

symbols.name: list_drafts
symbols.note: Returns a list of draft summaries, newest first.

symbols.name: get_draft
symbols.note: Returns a single draft by ID, or None.

symbols.name: delete_draft
symbols.note: Deletes a draft file by ID.

symbols.name: set_status
symbols.note: Updates the status of a draft, with validation and idempotency claim.

symbols.name: apply_payload
symbols.note: Returns a review packet for applying a draft and marks it as applied.

claims.text: An advisory-mode task legitimately writes nothing: the free lane produces a PROPOSAL that a write-capable, trusted lane (Claude / the user) applies later.
claims.why: The claim about advisory-mode tasks writing nothing is a design statement; this module only implements persistence of proposals. The code does not enforce that the free lane writes nothing, so the claim cannot be checked here.

claims.text: Until now that proposal lived only inside the offload result and evaporated when the caller dropped it. Here every accepted advisory report is persisted to ``runs/drafts/<ts>-<slug>.json`` so it can be listed, reviewed, applied, and cleaned up later.
claims.why: The module writes drafts to DRAFT_DIR (runs/drafts) with a timestamp-slug filename (line 56), and provides list, get, delete, and apply functions.

claims.text: Apply is deliberately NOT automated: a draft is a proposal, and the safety model says a free model may propose but never merge. Applying stays a human / Claude action.
claims.why: apply_payload() returns a packet and marks the draft as applied but does not perform any merge or write to the target repo (lines 92-105). The docstring of set_status also reiterates this (line 78).

claims.text: This module moved one package level deeper. Runtime state remains at the repository root for backward compatibility with every existing draft.
claims.why: ROOT is computed as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] (line 21), which points to the repository root (two levels up from the module file). DRAFT_DIR is under ROOT.

claims.text: A draft id is our own timestamp-slug stem. It arrives from the CLI and from URL path segments (/api/drafts/<id>/apply), so it MUST NOT be trusted into a filesystem path -- reject anything that isn't a plain stem (no separators, no traversal). Closes the path-traversal gap Minos would have flagged.
claims.why: _safe_path() validates the id with _ID_RE (line 33) which only allows alphanumeric, dot, underscore, hyphen, max 120 chars. Then it resolves the path and checks that it stays within DRAFT_DIR (lines 37-39).

claims.text: Resolve a draft id to its file ONLY if the id is a plain stem that stays inside DRAFT_DIR. Returns None for anything suspicious (``..``, separators, absolute paths, symlink escapes).
claims.why: The function first checks _ID_RE.match (line 33) to reject suspicious characters. Then it resolves the path and checks relative_to DRAFT_DIR (lines 38-39), which catches '..', absolute paths, and symlink escapes.

claims.text: Write one accepted advisory report to the drafts store; returns the path.
claims.why: The function writes a JSON file to DRAFT_DIR (line 66) and returns the path (line 67).

claims.text: never overwrite an existing draft from the same second
claims.why: After constructing the initial path, the code checks if it exists (line 60) and appends a counter if so (line 61).

claims.text: Newest-first summaries of every stored draft.
claims.why: The function sorts the glob results in reverse order (line 72), which gives newest first (assuming filenames start with timestamp).

claims.text: Transition a draft's lifecycle. Returns the updated draft, or None if the id is unknown; raises ValueError on an invalid status. This does NOT touch the filesystem of the target repo -- 'applied' only marks the proposal as handled (a free model may propose, never merge; the actual edit is a human / Claude action). Idempotent.
claims.why: The function checks status against _STATUSES and raises ValueError if invalid (line 82). It returns None if the draft doesn't exist (line 84). It only writes to the draft file, not the target repo (lines 86-90). The idempotency claim: the code always writes even if status is unchanged, but that doesn't break idempotency (the result is the same).

claims.text: The review packet a human / the Claude lane needs to ACTUALLY apply a draft: the objective, the target paths, and the proposal text. Marks the draft 'applied' (handled) but performs no write itself -- returning the packet IS the handoff. None if the id is unknown.
claims.why: The function calls set_status(draft_id, 'applied') (line 104) to mark the draft, and returns a packet with objective, paths, proposal, etc. (lines 97-103). It does not write to the target repo. Returns None if get_draft returns None (line 96).

observations.what: The regex _ID_RE allows '.' which could be a dotfile name, but since the path is resolved and checked relative to DRAFT_DIR, traversal is still blocked.
set_status does not check if the status is already the same; it still writes the file. This is not a bug but may be a minor inefficiency.
